props.heading: The Researcher & Artist
props.subheading: Blending the molecular chemistry of natural pigments with the art of traditional textiles.
props.col1: I am a PhD researcher and textile artist dedicated to tracing the histories, science, and geographies of natural pigments. My work bridges the gap between historical chemistry and traditional craft, exploring how ancient societies used native plants to color their world.
props.col2: Through field research and studio practice, I investigate the intricate fermentation of indigo, the earthy reds of madder, and the vibrant yellows of weld. This blog serves as a digital archive of these journeys, mapping the intersection of geography, science, and lived textile history.

props.quote: When an indigo vat breathes, it is not metaphor—it is billions of anaerobic bacteria reducing insoluble indigotin into liquid gold. The dyer's hand is simply an instrument of that living ecology.
props.author: Dr. E. Archer
